run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The cart workload is down: pod cart-74587775fc-4rnfw on node sregym-worker2 is in CrashLoopBackOff (5 restarts by 15:26:11) because its cart container aborts at startup with 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' thrown from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:101) via ValkeyCartStore.Initialize (line 71) at 15:22:40.9 and 15:22:46.95. The previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-4nht8 had logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 15:21:34.411 and was still serving GetCart/AddItem successfully up to 15:22:33; it was then stopped and replaced at 15:22:33, and the cart Service now has only a notReadyAddress (10.244.7.236:8080). The user-facing impact is verified: frontend logs show '13 INTERNAL: cart failure ... dial tcp 10.96.48.76:8080: connect: connection refused' and '14 UNAVAILABLE' from 15:22:36 to 15:22:55, frontend spans for POST /api/cart returned HTTP 500 with oteldemo.CartService/AddItem rpc.grpc.status_code=14, and Locust reported a 0.47 fail ratio with failures on GET/POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, while product-catalog and recommendation calls in the same window returned 200/status 0. The valkey-cart pod itself shows no own failure (Running, Ready, 0 restarts, 'Ready to accept connections tcp' since 15:21:27), so the deeper trigger is the cart->valkey reachability break that began between 15:22:34.978 (an init container in the very same cart pod reached 10.96.211.233:6379) and 15:22:40.9 (the app could not establish a Redis session); whether the cause is a network-level block on that path or valkey-cart ceasing to answer the Redis protocol is not resolvable with the available evidence, so the diagnosis is partial.

claims.text: Pod cart-74587775fc-4rnfw (namespace astronomy-shop, node sregym-worker2) is not Ready: container 'cart' is in state CrashLoopBackOff with restartCount 5 and last termination exitCode 139 reason 'Error' (finished 15:25:46Z); an earlier reading showed restartCount 2 with 'back-off 20s restarting failed container=cart'.

Cart container logs show the crash cause: 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with the stack at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 101) -> ValkeyCartStore.Initialize (ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 71) -> Program.Main (Program.cs:line 98), logged at 15:22:40.911Z (container attempt 0) and 15:22:46.951Z (attempt 1) for pod cart-74587775fc-4rnfw.

The previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-4nht8 was healthy until it was removed: it logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 15:21:34.411Z and served GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync successfully (cart spans POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and /AddItem with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and frontend /api/cart HTTP 200) up to 15:22:33, then logged 'Application is shutting down...'.

Kubernetes events show the cart pod was replaced: 'Stopping container cart' on pod cart-74587775fc-4nht8 at 15:22:33Z, ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc 'Created pod: cart-74587775fc-4rnfw' at 15:22:33Z, and the replacement pod's init container wait-for-valkey-cart logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.211.233:6379) open' at 15:22:34.978Z.

The cart Service has no ready backend: its Endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses 10.244.7.236:8080 targeting pod cart-74587775fc-4rnfw, while valkey-cart has a ready address 10.244.234.166:6379.

Frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-qrmbz logged repeated errors from 15:22:36Z to 15:22:55Z: 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.48.76:8080' and 'Error: 13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp 10.96.48.76:8080: connect: connection refused'.

Traces between 15:22:36Z and 15:22:56Z show frontend spans 'POST /api/cart' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' with error=true and http.status_code=500, and frontend client spans 'oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' with error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=14, grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.48.76:8080'; in the same window product-catalog GetProduct/ListProducts and recommendation ListRecommendations spans returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and frontend /api/products /api/recommendations returned HTTP 200.
The Locust exporter at 15:22:56Z reported locust_requests_fail_ratio 0.4737, with failures POST /api/cart = 4, GET /api/cart = 2, POST /api/checkout = 3, aggregated failures = 9.

valkey-cart shows no failure of its own: pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-kvdjs is Running with restartCount 0 and the valkey container logged '1:M 21 Nov 2026 15:21:27.374 * Ready to accept connections tcp' with no later restart; Deployment valkey-cart reports 1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available replica and defines no readiness or liveness probe.

Service definitions are consistent with the application configuration: Service cart (ClusterIP 10.96.48.76, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart) and Service valkey-cart (ClusterIP 10.96.211.233, port 6379 -> targetPort 6379, selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart); cart's VALKEY_ADDR env is valkey-cart:6379.

Nodes are healthy and DNS is up: sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3 and sregym-control-plane all report Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure/NetworkUnavailable=False, and the two CoreDNS pods (coredns-6b7b757f47-fpfll, coredns-6b7b757f47-trvr7) are Ready with restartCount 0, running since 14:42:08Z.

Rejected: an application feature-flag fault (e.g. cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe) being active. The flagd configuration ConfigMap demo.flagd.json shows every flag (cartFailure, paymentFailure, cart-related failedReadinessProbe, adFailure, emailMemoryLeak, etc.) with defaultVariant 'off'.

Rejected: cart container was OOMKilled or hit its memory limit (160Mi). Its working set was only 2,125,824 bytes and the termination reason/exit code recorded by kubelet is reason 'Error', exitCode 139 (SIGSEGV-style exit), not OOMKilled/137, and no Evicted or OOM event appeared for the cart pods.

Hypothesis (supported but not proven): the cart pod's path to valkey-cart was blocked at ~15:22:35Z. A process in the same pod and network namespace (init container wait-for-valkey-cart) completed a TCP connection to the valkey-cart ClusterIP 10.96.211.233:6379 at 15:22:34.978Z, yet the cart application failed to establish a Redis session 1-6 seconds later and kept failing through 15:26, while valkey's listener stayed up. This would explain a new pod failing where the previous pod's already-established session had worked.

Hypothesis (not excluded): valkey-cart stopped answering the Redis protocol after 15:22:34Z while its socket kept listening. Because Deployment valkey-cart defines no readiness/liveness probe, such a hang would leave the pod Ready with 0 restarts and no new log lines (only the 15:21:27 startup lines were observed until 15:22:56Z), and a client connection would then time out with exactly the 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' error the cart container logs.

Advisory follow-up: verify cart->valkey-cart reachability from inside the cart pod's network namespace (TCP and a Redis PING on 10.96.211.233:6379), and inspect Calico CRD network policy objects (crd.projectcalico.org NetworkPolicy/GlobalNetworkPolicy) plus any netem rules applied to pod cart-74587775fc-4rnfw's veth, because those cannot be read with the available read-only Kubernetes kinds and are the most likely place a path block would live.

Advisory follow-up: remove the cart container's hard startup dependency on an immediate Redis connection (retry with backoff instead of throwing) so a transient valkey-cart unavailability does not produce a CrashLoopBackOff, and add readiness/liveness probes plus a probe-visible health endpoint to cart and valkey-cart so a hung dependency or a non-serving container is detected instead of appearing Ready.

gaps: The mechanism that broke cart->valkey-cart connectivity at ~15:22:35Z is unresolved: the NetworkPolicy query for networking.k8s.io objects returned no objects (status no_data, not proof of absence) and Calico's crd.projectcalico.org NetworkPolicy/GlobalNetworkPolicy objects are not in the readable kind list, nor is change_history available, so no object applying a change or fault to the cart or valkey-cart pods was observed.

Whether valkey-cart was still answering the Redis protocol after 15:22:34Z is unknown: it has no probes, cart is its only client, and no command execution or Redis-level check is available; only the closed-state facts (Running, Ready, restartCount 0, startup log at 15:21:27) were observed.

Cart container logs after 2026-11-21T15:22:56Z (including the later crash attempts at 15:22:59, 15:23:28 and 15:25:46) are outside the authorized window and were dropped by log reads (13 lines after window end) and by the window filter, so the later crash messages were not read.

Prometheus returned no samples for traces_span_metrics_calls_total / traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_* and no app/rpc/http service metrics within the authorized window (series names exist but queries returned no data), so span-based error-rate and latency readings for cart and its callers are unknown rather than zero.

checkout's own failure was not verified: a Loki query on {app="checkout"} for error/fail/refused/unavailable/exception lines in 15:22:20-15:22:56Z returned no lines (status no_data), so the POST /api/checkout failures reported by Locust are not attributed to checkout's own logs.

No baseline exists for a latency comparison: the application pods were all scaled from 0 to 1 replica at 15:21:25-15:21:28Z, so the sampled window covers only the first ~90 seconds of this application instance and earlier 24h behaviour is unknown.
